pass_a_gloss: [...] my [portion] into a trackless desert. It became into a vanishing of destruction. And again: Because the shepherds acted foolishly and did not seek the Lord, because of this the whole pasture [flock] did not understand, and they were scattered. For the shepherds truly acted foolishly, and became a starting point of ruin for the peoples under hand. And yet how was it not needed rather that they, as having been very well instructed through law and prophets in the mystery of Christ, become a way for the others toward the need to believe in him? But, as the Saviour says, they were receiving glory from man, and the glory from the only God they were not seeking. For if they believed Moses, they would believe him; for that one wrote about him. They have become then blind and guides of blind. For this reason indeed they have slipped through, and have fallen into the pits of destruction. What then? The prophet tries to reshape them by good admonitions toward the need to choose to think the better things, and to make trial of the words of the Saviour. And he mixes usefully into the admonitions for this the rebuke, healing the wounds of the bad counsel in them as by a remedy all but variously prepared. For this reason, he says: Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; pay attention to law of God, people of Gomorrah. You hear how he brings upon peoples and rulers the rod from love and from a God-loving mind together, and strikes those very sick with the disobedient. And to the most impious cities he likens Jerusalem, as full of very much sin, and as having wholly no one in herself [gap in the printed text]; for the God of all was planning to burn the cities of the Sodomites, and he communicated the thing to Abraham; and he [said] to him: Will you destroy righteous with ungodly? And will the righteous be as the ungodly? And God was promising, if ten righteous should be found in Sodom, to restrain the wrath upon them. But they were not found. Therefore also they paid the penalties equal in measure to their own impieties. Such was the Lord-killing Jerusalem, having much scarcity of the righteous. And indeed the prophet Jeremiah was entreating about her. And God said: Run around in the streets of Jerusalem, and see and know, and seek in her squares, if you find a man, if there is one doing judgment and seeking faith, and I will be merciful to her, says the Lord. Since then, both filthy and stained in many ways with the defilements in baseness, and having much scarcity of the saints, he calls her Sodom and Gomorrah, and brings upon peoples and leaders the blame of the uncleanness of the Sodomites. And what does he say? Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom, pay attention to law of God, people of Go[morrah] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …“My portion into a trackless wilderness. It has been made a ruin of destruction” (Jeremiah 12:10–11). And again: “For the shepherds have acted foolishly and have not sought the Lord; therefore the whole flock has not understood, and they have been scattered” (Jeremiah 10:21). The shepherds truly acted foolishly, and became a cause of ruin for the peoples under their hand.

And yet should they not rather, as men thoroughly instructed in the mystery of Christ through the Law and the Prophets, have become a road for the others toward believing in Him? But, as the Savior says, they received glory from man and did not seek the glory that comes from the only God (John 5:44). “For if they had believed Moses, they would have believed Him, for he wrote about Him” (John 5:46). So they have become blind, and guides of the blind (Matthew 15:14). In this way, too, they have slipped and fallen into the pits of destruction.

What then? The prophet tries to reshape them with good admonitions, so that they would choose to think better things and make trial of the Savior's words. For this purpose he usefully mixes rebuke into his admonitions, healing the wounds of their bad counsel with what is almost a remedy of many ingredients. That is why he says: “Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; give heed to the law of God, you people of Gomorrah” (Isaiah 1:10). You hear how he brings down on peoples and rulers alike the rod that comes from love and from a godly mind, and strikes those gravely sick with disobedience.

He likens Jerusalem to the most impious cities, as one filled with a very great deal of sin and as having in herself no one at all [lacuna]. For the God of all was planning to burn the cities of the Sodomites, and He shared the matter with Abraham. Abraham said to Him: “Will You destroy the righteous with the ungodly? And shall the righteous be as the ungodly?” (Genesis 18:23). God promised that if ten righteous men were found in Sodom, He would hold back His wrath against them (Genesis 18:32). But they were not found. Therefore they paid penalties equal in measure to their own impieties. Such was Jerusalem, the slayer of the Lord, with her great scarcity of the righteous.

Indeed, the prophet Jeremiah pleaded earnestly for her, and God said: “Run through the streets of Jerusalem, and see, and know, and search in her squares, if you can find a man, if there is anyone who does justice and seeks faithfulness, and I will be merciful to her, says the Lord” (Jeremiah 5:1). Since, then, she is filthy, stained in many ways with the defilements of wickedness, and has a great scarcity of saints, he calls her Sodom and Gomorrah, and lays on peoples and leaders alike the reproach of the Sodomites' uncleanness. And what does he say? “Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; give heed to the law of God, you people of Go…” (Isaiah 1:10).

choices.english: as the Savior says, they received glory from man
choices.why: Cyril cites John 5:44 as the Saviour's words; it is not the Saviour who received glory.
rejected: Or does the Savior say that he received glory

choices.english: He would hold back His wrath against them
choices.why: God promised to restrain his wrath if ten righteous were found (Genesis 18:32).

choices.english: Jerusalem, the slayer of the Lord
choices.why: Cyril's polemical title, translated as written.
Admonition mixed with rebuke, like a compound medicine.
